notes: Drawn from OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (read 2026-10-08, © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL): every room, corridor and hall its mappers drew inside the building, at the outlines they drew, with the names and numbers they gave — level 0: 8 rooms, 10% of the model's floor at 0 m; level 1: 2 rooms, 1% of the model's floor at 5 m; level 2: 68 rooms, 64% of the model's floor at 10 m. Anchored on OpenStreetMap's coordinates; the model is guessed and is filed against them where it stands off. Levels between two (an entresol) and below the ground are not drawn. Each level's height is the site's: 5 m a level, the storey that gives the most of the mapped rooms headroom under the model's roof. Doorways: 30 where OpenStreetMap maps a door between two rooms; 42 by the rule where it draws two rooms side by side and no door, one of them otherwise without a way in (osm-rule). Between floors: 2 lifts where it maps a lift or a stair across levels, and one by the rule where it maps none. The way in: the rule (OpenStreetMap maps no entrance into its rooms here): the thinnest wall from a mapped room to open ground, cut into O-a3098732698. 75 of 76 rooms are reached from it. Nothing of it is the museum's own plan: where the museum's records name a room by a number OpenStreetMap gives, its works hang there; the rest are hung by the site, said so.
